newsitem.title: UK: EBRD SIGNS ENERGY EFFICIENCY DEAL FOR EAST EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: EBRD SIGNS ENERGY EFFICIENCY DEAL FOR EAST EUROPE.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said on Thursday it was financing a 50 million project to help eastern Europe stop its Communist-era equipment wasting so much fuel.
The project with Cie Generale de Chauffe (CGC), a subsidary of Cie Generale des Eaux , will develop a network of energy service companies in the region.
CGC will set up and operate the companies to provide energy-saving services to both the public and private sector, the Bank said.
They will recover the cost of installing the technology from the energy savings.

"By working with such companies as CGC, the EBRD can further develop a greater awareness of energy savings amongst consumers as well as establishing a private sector industry to support it," EBRD president Jacques de Larosiere said at the signing.
The Bank is also looking at similar deals with Swiss firm Landis & Gyr AG and Honeywell Inc .

"What we planning over the next four years or so is to set up a network of regional energy services. We hope it will be a snowballing process," Peter Hobson, the EBRD's principal banker for energy efficiency, told Reuters earlier.
"It's a great way of unlocking...this huge energy efficiency potential which is very difficult to realise through classical financial methods," he added.
Some of the prime targets will be state institutions such as hospitals and schools which do not have the money to update their equipment.
"They often have very old boiler systems, sometimes going back 50 years and no control systems and they wheeze and puff away. In some, it takes people stoking these things all day long," he said.
"They know they are wasting energy and they know they are paying for wasting energy, but they can't borrow the money to implement the technologies to save it," Hobson said.
"What the energy service companies can do is take on responsiblity for all of that in return for being paid out of the future energy savings."
The most recent figures, which are for 1992, show that the old East Bloc used a third more energy than the European Union for half the economic output.
Hobson estimated the market energy efficiency technology and equipment in the region was worth 50 billion.
